themes_detail.label: Street Conditions Crisis
themes_detail.summary: Street condition complaints exploded to 73 THIS WEEK, a 612% spike compared to the 10.2-complaint weekly average over the prior 8 weeks (z-score: 13.71), suggesting a sudden, district-wide deterioration in road quality that demands immediate investigation into what triggered this acute degradation.
evidence: 73 street condition complaints THIS WEEK vs. 10.2 weekly average over prior 8 weeks (612% increase)
Z-score of 13.71 indicates statistically extreme deviation
CB budget requests include road/infrastructure improvements, suggesting chronic underfunding
reporting_angles: Ground-truth reporting: Drive or walk streets in Washington Heights/Inwood to photograph and document specific potholes, cracked pavement, or other hazards generating complaints
Institutional accountability: Interview DOE, DOT, or local council member's office about what changed this week and response timeline

themes_detail.label: Park Noise Surge
themes_detail.summary: Park noise complaints jumped to 7 THIS WEEK, a 833% spike from the 0.8-complaint weekly average (z-score: 4.81), signaling either new heavy use patterns, events, or enforcement gaps in district parks that aligns with CB's long-standing request for enhanced park safety and security staff.
evidence: 7 park noise complaints THIS WEEK vs. 0.8 weekly average over 8 weeks (833% increase)
Z-score of 4.81 marks statistically significant spike
Community Board has repeated budget requests for enhanced park safety and security staff
reporting_angles: Park-by-park breakdown: Identify which Washington Heights/Inwood parks are generating complaints and speak with residents about timing and causes
Resource gap analysis: Examine whether Parks Enforcement or NYPD have reduced park patrol presence this week

themes_detail.label: Tree Damage & Illegal Cutting
themes_detail.summary: Illegal tree damage complaints spiked to 3 LAST WEEK (700% above the 0.4 average; z-score: 5.42) and damaged tree complaints hit 20 THREE WEEKS AGO (900% above 2.0 average; z-score: 4.69), suggesting either storm damage, contractor work, or organized illegal tree removal activity requiring environmental enforcement investigation.
evidence: 3 illegal tree damage complaints LAST WEEK vs. 0.4 weekly average (700% increase, z-score: 5.42)
20 damaged tree complaints 3 WEEKS AGO vs. 2.0 weekly average (900% increase, z-score: 4.69)
Pattern suggests either acute event (storm) or sustained removal activity
reporting_angles: Environmental crime angle: Investigate whether contractors or private parties are illegally removing street trees; check DOE/Parks violation records
Storm damage assessment: Determine if a weather event 2-3 weeks ago caused the spike and whether city cleanup is complete

themes_detail.label: Homelessness & Street Assistance
themes_detail.summary: Homeless person assistance complaints more than tripled to 14 LAST WEEK, a 286% spike compared to the 3.6-complaint weekly average (z-score: 5.2), indicating either a sudden increase in visible homelessness or a breakthrough in resident awareness/reporting of unmet needs in the district.
evidence: 14 homeless person assistance complaints LAST WEEK vs. 3.6 weekly average (286% increase, z-score: 5.2)
Timing suggests either new encampments or service gaps
CB budget requests for food assistance (SNAP) and social services suggest underlying need
reporting_angles: Boots-on-ground: Identify specific blocks or parks in Washington Heights/Inwood where homelessness is visible and map any new encampments
Service system angle: Interview Dept. of Social Services or outreach teams about whether new populations arrived or existing services declined

themes_detail.label: Bike Lane / Shared Space Complaints
themes_detail.summary: Bike/roller/skate complaints hit 3 LAST WEEK, a 2300% spike from the 0.1-complaint baseline (z-score: 8.69), possibly indicating new bike lane installations, conflicts between users, or enforcement activity that deserves clarification.
evidence: 3 bike/roller/skate complaints LAST WEEK vs. 0.1 weekly average (2300% increase, z-score: 8.69)
Low raw volume but extreme statistical deviation suggests novel activity or complaint type
reporting_angles: Infrastructure context: Check whether DOT installed new protected bike lanes or painted markings in the district recently
User conflict angle: Interview cyclists, skateboarders, and residents about friction points on shared streets or paths
